tasks.acceptance_prose:
Contract F-202 (OO core: ExcelFormat recalculates dependent cells on edit and writes the fresh value into the cached <v>). Model anchors: core/crates/wo-x2t/src/spreadsheet_model.rs:43 WoCell { r: "A1", t: 'n'/'s'/'b'/'str', v: value, s: style, f: Option<String> formula }. wo-sheet Cell { raw, value: CellValue, formula: Option<Expr> } at core/crates/wo-sheet/src/model.rs:111; wo-formula evaluates an AST with wo_formula::eval(expr, sheet) (trait Sheet with cell/range lookups) at core/crates/wo-formula/src/eval.rs:10. The xlsx -> wo-sheet read path resolves shared strings ONCE in the parser (converters.rs ~7059, F-201 fixed: never re-resolve t="s" indices; "Beta".parse::<usize>() corruption is resolved).

PROBLEM TO FIX (recalc-on-edit): a formula cell `<c><f>=A1*2</f><v>4</v></c>` keeps its cached <v> when the workbook is re-saved even after A1 changed — the cached value goes STALE and the output carries a lie.

YOUR DELIVERABLES (probe first, then implement):
1. Probe + regression test test_xlsx_recalc_on_edit: build a minimal xlsx (converters.rs test helpers exist: build_minimal_xlsx ~16906, build_two_string_xlsx ~16844) with A1=2 and B1=<f>=A1*2</f><v>4</v>. Edit A1 to 3 through the wo-sheet model (or directly via the xlsx converter path), convert back to xlsx, re-parse, and assert B1's cached <v> is 6 (recomputed), NOT 4 (stale).
2. Implement recalc in the write path: the sheet->xlsx serializer must, for every formula cell, recompute <v> from <f> against the current sheet values using wo_formula (converters.rs:7210/7319/7432 are the WoCell write arms that clone cell.f/formula). If evaluation errors or references are unresolved, OMIT <v> entirely (an absent cached value is honest; a stale one is a lie). Never write a stale <v>.
3. Regression test test_xlsx_cached_value_not_stale: after implementing, the probe above's behavior is locked in — B1 recomputed to 6 and a broken formula (e.g. =A1/0 or =NOPE()) serializes with f present but NO <v> (or a #DIV/0! error value, your choice, but assert exactly what you wrote and keep it deterministic).
4. F-204 preserve: add assertions to test_xlsx_recalc_on_edit that the edited workbook keeps r-addresses (A1/B1) and type letters (t='n') intact — address/type model must not be flattened during the edit+save.
5. F-203 calcChain decision: wo-x2t does NOT regenerate calcChain.xml on save (it is omitted on rewrite). That is now an explicit, documented contract: add a one-line comment in the sheet->xlsx writer stating 'calcChain.xml: omitted on rewrite — spreadsheet apps rebuild it lazily (F-203 decision documented 2026-10-10)'. Do NOT try to wire calcChain generation.
6. All existing wo-x2t tests must stay green.

Do NOT touch features.yaml (it lives in a different repository — the operator flips registry rows after your merge). Commit on the current branch with a conventional message naming the tests. Rust at /home/weiss/.cargo/bin, toolchain is nightly via rust-toolchain.toml.

tasks.title: Wysiwyg editor: page-width image fit + proportional drag-resize (width/height survive save)
tasks.acceptance_prose: The server now round-trips image dimensions (docx wp:extent <-> HTML width/height, committed 2026-10-10), so an with width/height attributes keeps its display size through save/reload. The editor (apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg/editor.js, flat vanilla JS, no build) currently does two things wrong: (a) a wide image renders at full pixel width overflowing the content column; (b) there is no drag-resize, so a user cannot scale a picture. DELIVERABLES, probe-first (write the test file BEFORE the feature, then implement until it passes): 1. Pure math in a testable form: implement TWO pure functions near the top of editor.js (module scope, referenced by name, no DOM): fitToWidth(naturalW, naturalH, maxW) -> {width, height} preserving aspect ratio (Math.round, never zero-size), and fitWithinPage(imgW, imgH, pageW, pageH) -> {width, height} scaling DOWN only (never upscale). 2. Create apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg/image-fit.test.mjs — a Node built-in test (node:assert, no framework, exit 0 on success) that: asserts fitToWidth(960,240,602) gives {602,150} (602/960*240=150.5 round -> 150 or 151, assert the exact round you implement), asserts fitWithinPage leaves a small image untouched (no upscale), asserts fitWithinPage scales a 960x240 banner into 602 or fewer px wide, and asserts aspect ratio is preserved within 1% for three sample pairs. Print the string 'IMAGE-FIT-PASS' at the end of a successful run. 3. Editor behavior: on load and on image insert (confirmImageDialog already writes width/height attributes from two inputs, editor.js ~1774), clamp: any whose natural width exceeds the content column width gets its width/height attributes set to fitToWidth(naturalW, naturalH, contentWidth) BEFORE the html is committed (do it in the same place the dialog builds dims, and also fix-up existing oversized imgs on document load). 4. Drag-resize: when an inside the editable content is selected, overlay a resize handle at its bottom-right corner; dragging it live-sets the img's width AND height attributes with fitToWidth-derived proportional values (src natural size as the base, canvas single-pixel mousemove, pointerup removes the handle and fires input/change so autosave captures the new attributes). Keep it dependency-free and self-contained — the file has no bundler or test runner; do not add npm dependencies and do not break the existing toolbar/dialog code. 5. style.css: img elements inside the editable content get max-width:100% as a safety net (never overflow the column). This is a real prod file WITHOUT a test harness — the only automated proof is the node test you add. The acceptance gate runs node --check plus your test file. Keep all existing editor features intact (grep for the dialog/table/heading code paths you touch; leave them working). Commit on the current branch with a conventional message. ABSOLUTE RULES: do not reformat/rewrite unrelated sections of the 307KB editor.js; minimal targeted edits only; no new files except the test; no npm deps. node is /usr/bin/node (v22, has node:assert and --test).
